This video is really making a big deal out of "no military"  when, in reality, they still have a military that functions as a military.... it is just called the "The Public Force". Just like the military would.• Costa Rica still has a National Public Security Council,  a National Intelligence and Securtiy Directorate and the Fuerza Elite (Elite Force).  BUT- you can't look up how much they are spending on this "non- military" military because in July 2026, President Laura Fernández and Public Security Minister Gerald Campos signed an executive decree—published in La Gaceta—placing a broad range of security and intelligence information, including budgets, contracts, and procurement, under a "State Secret" designation.
    while there is "no military" there are still dudes driving around in military vehicles, dressed in military garb and packing military weapons.....

comments.author: @michaelconnors8408
comments.text: I came to Costa Rica for 10 years before making the decision to finally retire here. The secret for me has been to buy a small house, and live pretty simply, which has been refreshing compared with life in the US, and more in line with how people here spend their lives. I live in the rural hills around lake Arenal, but close enough to Liberia for the things I want from the "big" city, and only 2 hours from several nice beaches when I get the urge. Cool and comfortable at 2000 ft, no air conditioning, lots of local fruits and vegetables which are very affordable, as the video mentioned. Stuff from the US is high, but I can pick and choose what's important. Living securely, and even comfortably, on a small pension. As the video says, anything imported is expensive, but not really necessary once you make the adjustment? All in all, I estimate that my cost of living here is about 40% less than the very affordable city in the US where I came from. The expats who come here, buy huge beach houses, and drive up prices are definitely a factor in Costa Rican life these days! But, they contribute a lot to the economy, and that's good for everyone, I suppose?
